theFOURMechanismsAssessedOneByOne: (1) ONE COERCION FUNCTION FOR INTEGERS -- ASSERTED, NOT VERIFIABLE. The generator is not retained. What is verifiable is its OUTPUT: every count in the file is a canonical decimal string matching ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$. I checked and it is. WOULD IT HAVE CAUGHT v3? Yes -- v3's integer entered as a copied source constant, and a coercion emitting a decimal string would have rendered it '1'.

(2) SOURCE-BOUNDARY COERCION RECORDING THE SOURCE'S JSON TYPE AS A STRING -- VERIFIED IN THE OUTPUT. All thirteen rows carry declaredValueJsonTypeInTheSOURCE as a string ('INT', 'STR', 'LIST'), and row 1 is the exact v3 defect site now carrying 'INT' as text and '1' as text. WOULD IT HAVE CAUGHT v3? Yes, at the only place the integer could enter.

(3) A STRICT PRE-SERIALIZATION WALK THAT RAISES -- CLAIMED, AND ITS PUBLISHED RESULT IS FALSE OF THIS FILE. It reports 2681 leaves against an emitted 2741. See B-EIR4-01 finding ONE. WOULD IT HAVE CAUGHT v3? Yes, IF it had run on the final object -- which by its own published figure it did not.

(4) RE-READ FROM DISK AND RE-WALK, PUBLISHED AS THE CENSUS -- THE CENSUS IS TRUE AND I REPRODUCED EVERY FIGURE IN IT. But this gate is a REPORT, not a gate: it runs after the file is on disk. It can detect, it cannot prevent.

theROUTEForANonStringLeaf.answer: YES, I FOUND ONE, AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL -- 60 LEAVES TRAVELLED IT IN THIS VERY FILE.
theROUTEForANonStringLeaf.theRoute: Any value appended to the object AFTER gate1 runs and BEFORE json.dump. Gate1 is the only mechanism claimed to make a non-string leaf unemittable, and it demonstrably did not see the final object. A non-string leaf inserted into that window -- for example into the very census section that reports the gate results -- would reach json.dump unchallenged by gate1, and would be caught only by gate5, after the file exists.
theROUTEForANonStringLeaf.whyThisIsNotMerelyTheoretical: The window is 60 leaves wide, it is 2.2 percent of the artifact, and on the only arithmetic that closes it contains the entire emittedFileLeafCensus section. That section's values cannot pass through the source-boundary coercion of mechanism (2), because they are not source values -- they are the generator's own measurements of itself.
theROUTEForANonStringLeaf.aSECONDSmallerBlindSpotIRecordButDoNOTFi: A LEAF WALK IS BLIND TO EMPTY CONTAINERS. MEASURED: v4 contains FOUR empty JSON arrays -- testVectors.R-2-universeCommitment.vectors[0].members, R-3...vectors[0].outcomes, R-4...vectors[0].subjects and R-1...vectors[2].rawProofInventoryItems. Each is a JSON value that is not a string and contributes ZERO leaves, so neither the strict walk nor the census can see it. This does NOT violate numericRepresentationRule as written -- an empty array is not a number, boolean or null, and it is not a leaf -- and the four instances are all legitimate empty-set test inputs. I record it because the rule's enforcement is leaf-scoped and its blind spot should be known.
theROUTEForANonStringLeaf.aTHIRDLimitOfTheReReadGate: json.dump silently coerces integer, boolean and None object KEYS to strings. So a non-string KEY surviving gate1 would be invisible to gate5's re-read, which sees only the coerced string keys on disk. nonStringObjectKeys '0' is therefore a true statement about the BYTES that cannot testify about the OBJECT. The bytes are what is published, so this is a limit rather than a defect.

adjudications.subject: v4 against itself: 'The gates run at write time, once, in a process nobody can re-execute. A reviewer can verify the properties they produced; it cannot verify that they ran.' Is a self-certifying artifact with unreproducible gates acceptable as a candidate? Section 7.1 grades the no-retained-checker residual disqualifying for APPLICATION, and this is the same shape one level in.
adjudications.ruling: YES, THE BOUND IS ACCEPTABLE FOR A CANDIDATE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT I REJECT THIS ARTIFACT FOR. BUT THE BOUND IS NARROWER THAN v4 THINKS, AND v4 SHELTERS TWO FALSE FIGURES BEHIND IT.
whyTheBOUNDIsAcceptableInPrinciple: A CANDIDATE IS NOT AN APPLICATION. Section 7.1's no-retained-checker residual is disqualifying for APPLICATION because an applied surface must stay true as the corpus moves. A candidate binds nothing, and v4 correctly states it binds nothing, applies nothing and closes no row. The two grades are not the same grade.

THE ALTERNATIVE IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THIS LEVEL. A retained checker for this artifact would itself be a program whose own execution a reviewer must trust; the regress does not terminate in a document. What terminates it is REPRODUCIBLE PROPERTIES, and v4 supplies those: the census, the byte length, the grep counts, the totals and every digest are all independently recomputable, and I recomputed them.

IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN CONCEALED. theHONESTLimitOfAllFive says the gates 'are not a retained checker and they are not offered as one'. Concealing that would be the section 7.2.2 defect. Disclosing it is the correct move and v4 makes it unprompted.

THE PROPERTIES ARE WHAT BIND, NOT THE PROCESS. v4 states the right test itself: 'A reviewer cannot verify the gates; it can only verify the properties they were supposed to produce. So verify those, and treat the claims about the generator as unverified prose.' That is the correct standard and I applied it.

butTheBOUNDDoesNOTCoverWhatV4UsesItFor.theDistinction: THERE IS A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A CLAIM A REVIEWER CANNOT CHECK AND A CLAIM A REVIEWER CAN CHECK AND FIND FALSE. The bound licenses the first. It does not license the second.
butTheBOUNDDoesNOTCoverWhatV4UsesItFor.applied: 'The strict walk raised on the first non-string leaf' is unverifiable and is properly covered by the bound. 'It passed at 2681 leaves' is a NUMBER ABOUT THIS FILE, and this file has 2741 leaves. 'unquotedOccurrences: 0' is a NUMBER ABOUT THESE BYTES, and these bytes yield 12. Both are falsifiable and both are false. No bound about unreproducible processes rescues a figure that contradicts the artifact carrying it.
butTheBOUNDDoesNOTCoverWhatV4UsesItFor.andTheSECTIONSaysSoItself: emittedFileLeafCensus.whatThisIs declares the whole section to be a census 'OF THE BYTES ON DISK, not of the object in memory'. v4 chose that scoping. Two of the figures inside it do not meet it.

adjudications.theSHAPEComparisonIsAptButCutsTheOtherWa: The brief is right that this is the no-retained-checker shape one level in. But the section 7.1 residual is disqualifying for application precisely because nothing NOTICES when the world moves. Here something did notice: I did, by recomputing. The write-time-gate design is acceptable exactly to the extent that its outputs are recomputable and recomputed. v4's failure is not that the gates are unreproducible -- it is that two of their published outputs were never compared against the file they describe, which is the ONE check the design's own logic requires.
adjudications.theGENERALRuling: A self-certifying artifact with unreproducible gates is an acceptable CANDIDATE when every gate publishes a property the reviewer can recompute, and when every such property is true of the emitted bytes. The first condition is met here. The second is not, at two figures. Fix those two and the design stands.
adjudications.andIRecordTheDESIGNIsAnImprovement: The move from v3 to v4 -- from measuring beside the emit path to gating the emit path -- is the right direction and the right diagnosis of B-EIR3-01. I am rejecting the execution of one gate's reporting, not the architecture.
